jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Data-Driven Circular Manufacturing and Digital Product Passports - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Are you driven by the challenge of making industrial manufacturing genuinely circular — and do you have the analytical and practical skills to make it happen? 

We are looking for an exceptional PhD candidate to work at the cutting edge of data-driven design, circular manufacturing, and digital product passports.

The position is primarily affiliated with the Section of Design for Sustainability (DfS) at DTU Construct, which has an internationally recognised track record in sustainable design and manufacturing, circular economy, digital product passports and life cycle assessment. DTU Construct also hosts the Danish National Center for Remanufacturing (reManuFactory), providing direct access to a unique ecosystem of 150+ Danish manufacturing companies and a host of other researchers. You will be an active member of this centre and will collaborate regularly with ongoing projects in the DfS section, including:

• 
3D-VALUE (Circularity Value Visibility Driving Co-Creation Through Circular-by-Design Products and Servitization), a three-year international research and innovation project funded by the EUREKA Circular Value Creation programme and the Innovation Fund Denmark (IFD)

• 
bi0SpaCE (Industry 4.0 Enhanced Digital Product Passports and Circular Economy Dataspaces for Sustainable Bio-Based Industries) funded by the Horizon Europe programme.

A secondary affiliation is expected with the Advanced Manufacturing Engineering Group at Grundfos A/S. In this capacity, you will contribute directly to the core research at the interface of design, manufacturing, circularity and data, working closely with Grundfos A/S — a world leading pump manufacturer — to advance methods for data-driven circularity and sustainability assessment in real industrial settings. You are expected to contribute to the development of new methods and tools that allow OEMs such as Grundfos A/S to design products from the outset for circular strategies such as reuse, refurbishment, and remanufacturing.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your primary responsibilities will focus on activities related to the development of (digital) life cycle data infrastructure and techniques for assessing and maximising circular value creation. 

Your primary tasks include:

• 
Develop a methodological cornerstone for circular product design using data embedded in digital product passports, synthesising insights on design for remanufacturing, circular customisation, and data-driven sustainability assessment into a unified framework.

• 
Develop data-driven algorithms and ML/AI pipelines for circular product development with direct application to (re-)manufacturing. This includes building pipelines that use, e.g., operational data from manufacturing and use-condition life cycle data to guide decisions that maximise value retention at end-of-use.

• 
Advance life cycle data collection, representation and visualisation methods for supporting sustainability- and circularity-guided quantitative decision-making in OEMs.

• 
Produce and publish high-quality scientific manuscripts in top-tier peer-reviewed journals and contribute to the dissemination of results at major international conferences.

• 
Participate in knowledge transfer activities, including a local in-person training event targeting Danish SMEs, and contribute to the validation of the developed methods.

The ideal candidate has a strong foundation in mathematical modelling and is passionate about applying advanced computational methods to engineering design and sustainable manufacturing. A prior background in building and maintaining a well-structured codebase (e.g., in Python, MATLAB, C++) is a plus. 

Candidates are encouraged to highlight all relevant experiences in their application, especially,

• 
Using computational methods in engineering design, e.g., design optimisation, simulation-driven design, digital twin development.

• 
Research/projects on three-dimensional data analysis, geometric modelling, and computer-aided engineering in a computational context.

• 
Knowledge on concepts such as remanufacturing, design for disassembly, or digital product passports.

• 
Prior background in circularity assessment and life cycle assessment (LCA) methods, applied to products and manufacturing systems.

• 
Research outputs, such as peer-reviewed conference papers, journal articles, or equivalent research contributions such as a high-quality MSc thesis.

We are primarily looking for candidates with a background in mechanical/industrial engineering, engineering design, computer science, or applied mathematics, although we welcome applications from other disciplines where the required skills are demonstrated.

Furthermore, you are intellectually curious, comfortable working across disciplinary boundaries, and motivated by translating research into real industrial impact. You write and speak English fluently. You thrive in collaborative, international environments and have the independence to drive your own research agenda while engaging closely with industrial and academic partners.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by the project team at the Section of Design for Sustainability, DTU Construct, based on qualifications, relevant experience, demonstrated research output, and motivation for the project. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is 1 March 2027, or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Dev Ramanujan, devr@dtu.dk (please mention “PhD Position Enquiry 3DV” in your email subject).

You can read more about DTU Construct at https://construct.dtu.dk/ and about the National Center for Remanufacturing at DTU at https://remanufactory.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 January 2027 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• 
A letter motivating the application (cover letter)

• 
Curriculum vitae

• 
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

• 
An optional publication list with DOIs and, for each, one sentence describing your specific contribution

• 
An optional list with links to projects and/or code repositories you have developed with a short note on your specific contribution

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

The research within the Section of Design for Sustainability (DfS) is driven by the need to integrate sustainability considerations into systems, the built environment, products and services, within companies and society, plus the need to ensure the design of sustainable production and consumption systems. The Section’s research combines deep theoretical studies with highly applied action research methodologies, aiming at contributing both to basic knowledge on Design for Sustainability and to ensure its implementation into industry and society, at large.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Power System Engineer for Dynamics, Modelling and Control; DK - Fredericia
jobs.description:
The Danish power system is changing rapidly as wind, solar, batteries, power electronics and international connections play an increasingly important role. This creates new dynamic behaviour and calls for better models, analysis methods and engineering tools. As our new Power System Engineer, you help us understand these changes and turn complex analyses into practical solutions. You also help develop and maintain the simulation environment that supports our stability studies and engineering decisions.

“We are looking for someone who enjoys building models and tools while keeping sight of the physical power-system problem they are intended to solve. A structured approach to maintenance, quality and processes is just as important as developing new solutions.”
– Laurids Dall, Manager

Join an international team of power-system specialists
At our head office in Fredericia you join a highly specialised and international team working with power-system dynamics, stability and power quality. We support system operation, contribute to major technical projects and identify the capabilities the future power system will need. Close technical collaboration is an important part of our work, and we therefore expect you to work from the office at least two days a week.

Shape the tools behind a stable power system and enhance our simulation environment

Your tasks depend on your experience and the projects you join. You will typically:

• Perform dynamic stability studies and identify present and future system needs.
• Develop and validate dynamic models and analysis methods.
• Develop, maintain and quality-assure our simulation environment, primarily using DIgSILENT PowerFactory and PSCAD.
• Automate simulations, screening and analysis workflows.
• Translate technical findings into recommendations for system design and operation.

The job combines power-system engineering with structured development and maintenance. You help ensure that models, processes and results are documented, reproducible and suitable for reuse across the organisation. 

Within your first 6–12 months, we expect you to have:

• Contributed professionally to stability studies or model-development activities.
• Understood the structure and purpose of our simulation environment.
• Improved at least one model, workflow or quality-assurance process.
• Turned analysis results into clear technical conclusions.
• Build effective working relationships within the team and across Energinet.

Combine technical curiosity with a structured approach

You have a MSc in electrical engineering or a related field. Your academic or professional background may include electrical power systems, power-system dynamics, power electronics, converter control or electrical energy systems. You may be a recent graduate or have a few years of relevant experience. We do not expect you to know every part of the field from day one. What matters is your technical foundation, willingness to learn and ability to approach complex engineering problems systematically. 

You check off one or more of the qualifications we are looking for:

• Dynamic modelling and stability analysis in DIgSILENT PowerFactory or PSCAD/EMTDC
• RMS or EMT simulation
• Programming, scripting or automated engineering workflows
• Model validation, documentation and quality assurance
• Version control or collaborative software-development practices

Often the problems we work with do not have a predefined solution. You should therefore enjoy investigating complex technical questions, challenging assumptions and developing new approaches together with others. You will thrive in the role if you:

• Are curious and want to understand why a system behaves as it does.
• Enjoy building models and tools while keeping sight of the problem they are intended to solve.
• Can structure complex problems, turn analysis into practical conclusions and take responsibility for progressing your own work.
• Enjoy collaborating and sharing knowledge with other specialists as well as communicating complex topics to colleagues with different technical backgrounds.

Will you make a difference with us?

We look forward to receiving your motivated CV no later than 20 December. You may want to pencil in a couple of dates in your calendar already. We expect the first interview to take place online on 5 January and the second interview in Fredericia on 11 January.
If you have questions about the job, please contact Manager Laurids Dall on
tel. +45 3092 3194.

Special conditions: As Energinet performs tasks critical to society, we carry out background checks prior to employment. Employment is conditional upon your background check being compatible with employment at Energinet. The background check is also carried out once a year.
The position also requires that you are able to obtain and maintain security clearance. On PET's website, you can read more about security clearance.

We see diversity as a strength and encourage all qualified people, regardless of background, to apply for the job. We work actively and determinedly with diversity in Energinet and therefore encourage you to exclude information about age, marital status, etc. to minimise outage biases in the process. You can read more about our diversity policy here.

Energinet Systemsansvar's core tasks are to integrate renewable energy, ensure equal access to the grids, develop market design, monitor, and balance the transmission grid and ensure security of supply in Denmark. We are a subsidiary of the Energinet Group, which represents the interests of society when supplying Denmark with electricity and gas and that the energy system is converted to green energy. Our culture is closely linked to our social responsibility, and we work actively with the UN's global goals on sustainable energy, climate action, partnerships for action as well as industry, innovation, and infrastructure. By leading the way in the green transition, we can help to solve the global climate challenge. New solutions require us to be able to see problems from many different angles, and diversity is therefore a keyword in our culture. We strive to listen to, involve and share our knowledge. Based on the values of courage and trust, we focus on constantly developing ourselves as an organisation and as people. Read more at our website www.energinet.dk.

jobs.occupation: DIAS Fellow in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invite applications for a tenure-track DIAS Fellow position at Assistant Professor level in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment, with a focus on input-output life cycle assessment methods and big data. The candidate is expected to start during the summer/early fall in 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, in agreement with the successful candidate. 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Who are we looking for?

The position translates this ambition into a concrete research agenda, because many of the most pressing sustainability questions, such as how consumption in one country drives resource use, emissions and social conditions in another, or how a new technology changes environmental impacts across whole economies, cannot be answered within a single discipline. Industrial ecology addresses these questions by tracing material, energy and monetary flows through global supply chains, drawing on methods and data from engineering, economics and the natural and social sciences. Input-output analysis, built on big data covering production, trade, emissions and resource use and combined with life cycle assessment and material flow analysis, provides the quantitative framework for linking decisions about individual products, technologies and policies to their economy-wide consequences. The Fellow will build this capacity at SDU and use DIAS as a platform to work with researchers in fields such as health, food, energy, economics and political science on questions that cross disciplinary boundaries. Within this ambition, the specific profile is as follows.

We seek an early-career researcher who will advance quantitative sustainability assessment within industrial ecology by developing data-driven environmental-economic and systems models that link global production and consumption to environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. The role includes independent research, research-based teaching and supervision, interdisciplinary collaboration across DIAS and the Department, and development of competitive external funding proposals. Relevant research themes include:

·         environmental and material footprinting of global production and consumption systems;

·         development and application of environmentally extended input–output (EEIO) and multi-regional input–output (MRIO) models and databases, including hybrid physical–monetary systems and transparent, reproducible data workflows;

·         hybrid modelling that combines EEIO analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA), material flow analysis (MFA), econometrics or other quantitative methods;

·         applications to food and resource systems, healthcare systems and medical technologies, the circular economy, energy, infrastructure and other societal systems; and

·         scenario, structural decomposition, uncertainty and econometric analysis for sustainability transitions, policy and decision support.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

·         A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

·         A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields.

·         Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

·         Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must:

·         Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of industrial ecology, environmental or ecological economics, environmental science or engineering, sustainability science or a closely related field. To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

·         The successful candidate should demonstrate strong competence in EEIO or MRIO analysis, and at least one of the following areas: LCA, MFA, or hybrid modelling; econometric, statistical, or other quantitative methods; and programming, data science, or management of large, heterogeneous datasets.

·         Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries.

·         Be fluent in English.

·         Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

·         Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.   

The Department of Green Technology

The Department of Green Technology at SDU is a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment focused on developing technologies and strategies for a sustainable future. Our research spans environmental chemistry, process engineering, life cycle thinking, and circular systems. We collaborate closely with industry and public stakeholders to ensure real-world impact and relevance.

This position will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering (SDU LCE).

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

SDU LCE uses industrial ecology approaches to reduce environmental impacts and reconcile human development with environmental stewardship. We conduct holistic systems analyses and design studies to characterise and optimise engineering solutions over the long term, considering resource use, energy efficiency, climate and environmental impacts, and economic and socioeconomic performance. At SDU LCE, we develop and apply theory, methods and tools for material flow analysis (MFA), life cycle assessment (LCA), life cycle engineering, energy-system analysis and design, resource-criticality assessment, process integration and techno-economic assessment.

 

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For further information about SDU Life Cycle Engineering and this position, please contact Head of Centre, Professor Morten Birkved, at morb@igt.sdu.dk.

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and the provisions for tenure track assistant professor as described herein. Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please see Further information on salary and taxation.

 

The tenure track programme is aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area.

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level (up to six years) and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.  This evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential.

Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. The evaluation may also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities. 

As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution.

The programme includes annual performance reviews, a midterm evaluation by an expert panel, and a final academic assessment. If the final assessment is positive, the candidate will progress to a permanent position as associate professor. If the final evaluation is negative, the assistant professor may request one additional assessment within the last six months of employment. The tenure track period may be extended in connection with maternity, paternity, or adoption leave.

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

Please go to our website for full information on how to apply.

The application deadline is February 28, 2027, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)
